constructors.title: Crossed plant identity and organ class require two separately reused arguments
constructors.constructor: PART_CLASS(organ_class, plant_kind) versus NAME(plant_kind) versus PROPERTY(attribute, owner). These are hypothetical type contracts, not new glosses.
constructors.observable_written_consequence: Across a same-plant whole/fragment relation, the plant-kind argument remains fixed while organ extent may change. Across different plants sharing an independently classified organ, an organ-class argument can remain fixed while plant-kind changes. One frozen finite construction must account for both crossings rather than give each label an unrelated whole value.
constructors.minimum_case: Two singular same-kind whole/part relations on separate development leaves and at least one definite different-kind/same-organ contrast among already fixed neighboring fragments. All designated relations and neighboring alternatives remain; no matching subset is selected. This capacity is not asserted from unseen1126 observations.
constructors.falsifier: The fixed NAME-only contract requires one kind but assigns different kinds to a supported same-kind relation, or the fixed PART_CLASS contract assigns the same bound organ argument to demonstrably different organ classes without its declared modifier. A mismatch rejects that exact contract, not all contextual names.
constructors.meaning_decision: Tests whether a shared constituent carries a plant-kind argument, an organ-class argument or neither. It cannot select ROOT, a botanical species or an English property without an independent semantic anchor.
unknowns: No morphology, organ classification, owner endpoint or crossed cell is supplied here.
Register-conditioned allomorphy and exact-whole residuals must be frozen and charged; not inferred after a conflict.
Different silhouettes or different drawing complexity alone do not establish different botanical kinds; that crossing may remain unavailable.
constructors.likely_failure: Every crossing can be paid away as a separate whole name or a register variant unless the finite shared argument construction is fixed before writing the model.
retained_primary_stops: GDT352 rejects exact/family invariance in the singular f96v/f99r relation.
SNPL002 and redundant1084 fail same four relation/24assignment motif recovery.
1088/1089 broad organ resemblance is not species diagnosis or confirmed head meaning.

constructors.title: Owner-bound part reference differs from a free-standing organ-kind label
constructors.constructor: A binary owner-bound mention PART_OF(p,w) carries an explicit plant-owner argument; ORGAN_KIND(c) names a class without selecting that owner. The opposite phrasing HAS_PART(w,p) is the same relation under inversion and is not a semantic rival.
constructors.observable_written_consequence: Where the complete row contains two different plant owners with similar organ classes, the reference constructor must bind each part to its own written owner without nearest-label or latest-topic fallback. Switching the owner endpoint changes the truth of PART_OF even though organ shape/kind is unchanged. The generic organ label supplies no such unique-owner claim.
constructors.minimum_case: One complete already fixed row with at least two singular fragment-label ownerships plus the corresponding complete owned plant contexts. Root must establish the endpoints; their existence or meanings are not asserted here. A kind-level drawing correspondence never establishes numerical identity of specimens.
constructors.falsifier: A fixed owner-reference rule selects the neighboring plant, leaves two equally eligible owners or crosses unknown content capable of replacing the owner. UNKNOWN prevents a decisive result; it is not a donor.
constructors.meaning_decision: Can reject an exact independent-label constructor only if the text actually commits to a distinct owner relation. Mere proximity or same label form cannot decide generic class versus owner-bound mention.
unknowns: Owner-relative morphology and a written binding rule are missing.
Native image ownership supplies an inscription-to-fragment owner, not a word-to-plant semantic argument.
No individual identity or patient carry follows from shared source-kind.
constructors.likely_failure: An author donates the pictured plant as an implicit argument and makes the free class label relational by fiat; the two models then have the same consequence.
retained_primary_stops: GDT352 ambiguous f100r.3 offset/common AQJAC cannot select label owner.
GA068 remains untested; repeated kind does not establish individual identity.
669 requires complete text-to-drawing owner and directed content, not name-root similarity.

constructors.title: A property assertion needs a written owner and truth scope; a qualified name does not assert a new state
constructors.constructor: ASSERT(P,x) versus REFER(QUALIFIED_KIND(P,K)); a part referent and its parent plant are different possible x. A shared formal constituent is not assigned P here.
constructors.observable_written_consequence: A fixed property predicate must take the same licensed argument type wherever reused and keep its owner scope: a clause about a pictured fragment cannot silently assert the property of the whole plant, or conversely. A written condition or denial, if independently bound, operates on the assertion; a nominal restriction denotes a qualified kind and does not itself establish that condition at a new time.
constructors.minimum_case: One complete owned same-plant whole/part pair with a reused finite family and an actual written predicate/condition/denial construction whose scope is constrained independently of the proposed property word. No such construction is claimed currently; anatomy alone cannot provide it.
constructors.falsifier: The frozen predicate is applied to an incompatible argument or changes owner/time without written scope. Conversely, if both models simply describe the same qualified entity, there is no distinguishing consequence and no test should start.
constructors.meaning_decision: Distinguishes a fixed predicative commitment from a naming/restrictor commitment only when assertion scope has a consequence. Does not rank a species-name versus property gloss from morphology or frequency alone.
unknowns: No P, copula, tense, negation or condition value is donated.
Drawn omission does not assert a negative property.
Shared part grammar requires exact-whole residuals and entry-context accounts; no universal suffix semantics.
constructors.likely_failure: A nominal description embeds the property, or assertion truth is never independently constrained; both constructions fit the same content after renaming.
retained_primary_stops: GDT768 flower/seed direction ties; dry/moist apparent affinity fails family ablation, so no property polarity inherited.
GDT1115 FORM/TRANS final-line hypotheses may describe the same outcome and remain unranked.
1088 kooiin organ disagreement and pchor inconsistent triple prohibit automatic organ/property naming.

constructors.title: Static part selection differs from an executed separation with a retained-material effect
constructors.constructor: SELECT_OR_DESCRIBE_PART(w,p) versus EXECUTE_SEPARATION(w,p,remainder). An anatomical whole/part relation can support the former without any event or chronology.
constructors.observable_written_consequence: The execution constructor owes a written operation, its source participant and a fixed retained/discarded organ effect; the static constructor owes a part description/reference but no changed state. If a complete frozen execution destroys all recognizable organs in the same retained material, it cannot simultaneously identify that material as a recognizable pictured organ endpoint under an independently fixed terminal-stage relation.
constructors.minimum_case: One complete owned plant-context/fragment pair plus a genuinely written action/state relation and an independently owned image-stage or endpoint role.1126 can at most establish anatomical relation capacity; it cannot supply execution/time by itself.
constructors.falsifier: A complete fixed operation deletes the organ positively present at the same bound terminal stage, with no written restoration or separate stock. If timing/participant/organ effect is UNKNOWN, result is missing binding; not preservation, incompatibility or PASS.
constructors.meaning_decision: Can reject a specific terminal-production interpretation while retaining static catalogue/initial depiction. Physical part difference alone cannot establish a harvesting or preparation meaning.
unknowns: No cutting, extraction, storage, dose or treatment gloss is assigned.
A drawing simplification is not an observed extraction.
No inferred absence, new stock, hidden branch or semantic repair allowed.
constructors.likely_failure: The fragment is an identification/source-kind illustration rather than the final material, or the whole text never binds the operator/organ effect.

why_morphology_cannot_select_species_vs_: Directed composition establishes ordered reusable structure, not the argument type or referential truth of a constituent. The same stem/affix family can be a species-name family, organ-class restriction, property construction or native register/layout variation; exact whole residuals remain informative. A native whole/part relation constrains the nonlinguistic relation only. It does not decide whether an inscription names the parent kind, depicted part, state, use or a record field. Controlled crossing and actual written owner/scope duties can falsify fixed versions, but do not by themselves select English names.
